newsitem.title: FRANCE: S&P raises ratings on Scor.
newsitem.headline: S&P raises ratings on Scor.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Monday it had raised its senior unsecured and claims paying ability ratings of French reinsurer Scor to AA minus from A plus.
The ratings agency said in a statement that it had also boosted Scor's commercial paper rating to A1 plus from A1.

It said the upgrade reflected the group's increasingly diversified sources of earnings and improved financial flexibility. Other positive factors included Scor's position as a leading global reinsurer, strong technical expertise, excellent capitalisation and good operationg performance, it said.

However, S&P said offsetting these positive factors was the agency's belief that debt leverage was "still somewhat aggressive and that the current downturn in the reinsurance cycle may impede earnings".
It said the 1997 underwriting result was likely to show a certain degree of deterioration due to further rate softening.

But it said Scor's conservative underwriting approach and its more diversified source of earnings in the absence of a major catastrophic event should help maintain a satisfactory operating performance.
However, if the rate softening prevails, the group's 10 percent to 12 percent return on earnings target may be difficult to maintain beyond 1997, S&P said.
The AA- claims paying ability rating also includes Scor Reinsurance, General Security Property and Casualty Co, General Security Insurance Co, among others, S&P said.
